overview: IAM roles give AWS services permissions to act on your behalf, so applications on AWS do not need stored user credentials. Two audit tools review IAM: the account-level Credentials Report and the user-level Access Advisor. The best-practice list summarises the whole IAM chapter and is heavily tested.

coreConcepts.definition: An identity with permissions that AWS services can use to perform actions on your behalf.
A role assigned to an EC2 instance so its applications can access AWS.
Account-level report listing all users and the status of their credentials.
User-level view of service permissions granted and when each was last accessed.

mustRemember: Some AWS services need to perform actions on your behalf; give them permissions with IAM roles.
Common roles: EC2 instance roles, Lambda function roles, roles for CloudFormation.
Credentials Report = account level; Access Advisor = user level.
Use Access Advisor's last-accessed data to revise and tighten policies.
Best practice: one physical user = one AWS user.
Best practice: assign users to groups and permissions to groups.
Best practice: strong password policy and enforced MFA.
Best practice: use roles for AWS services and access keys for programmatic access (CLI/SDK).
Never share IAM users or access keys.

keyComparisons.difference: Report: all users' credential status account-wide. Advisor: one user's permitted services and last access.
A user is a person with long-term credentials; a role is assumed by a service to act on your behalf.

commonMisunderstandings: Access Advisor does not list every user's credential status; that is the Credentials Report.
Roles are not a replacement for one user per person; they give services permissions.
mentalModels: A role is a hat an AWS service puts on to get permissions; it does not belong to a person.

whenToUse.situation: An application on EC2 must read from S3
Find users without MFA or with old access keys
Remove permissions a user never uses

patternsToRecognize.signal: A service needs to act on your behalf
Services last accessed by a user

examTraps.trap: Store access keys on an EC2 instance for its application
examTraps.correction: Attach an IAM role to the instance.

examTraps.trap: Access Advisor lists all users and their credential status
examTraps.correction: That is the IAM Credentials Report.

examTraps.trap: Assign permissions directly to every user
examTraps.correction: Assign users to groups and permissions to groups.

beyondSource: Roles provide temporary credentials that rotate automatically, which is why they are preferred over access keys on AWS compute.
